newsitem.title: KENYA: Dunlop boosts Nairobi bourse turnover.
newsitem.headline: Dunlop boosts Nairobi bourse turnover.

text.p: A single lot of 55,000 shares of Dunlop Kenya traded across books on the one-hour hold board boosted turnover at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Thursday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The NSE 20-share index gained 21.17 points to 3055.97. Turnover was posted at 24.349 million shillings traded on 370,114 shares from 8.615 million shillings traded on 339,350 shares on Wednesday.
"Activity on the normal boards was moderate. Turnover was boosted by the single lot of Dunlop which made for 14.3 million shillings of total turnover," a bourse official said.
"Dunlop Kenya are high value shares, scarce and rarely traded," a senior broker said. Currently Dunlop is trading cum-dividend, the dividend being 20.975.
"Anybody wanting to dispose his shares in such big quantities must be doing so at a premium because he is foregoing his dividend to make a profit on his initial investment," the broker added.

On average, prices of key shares were stable with marginal price gains. Uchumi Supermarket gained 2.0 from 48.50 50, Nation Printers and Publishers traded at 106 from 105 while Barclays Bank traded at 97 from 96.50.
There was continued interest in Kenya Breweries where a foreign investor bought 22,200 shares at 50.
"Traditionally, Kenya Breweries has been a good investment for foreigners. Their books are about to close and they are trading cum-dividend," a broker said.
He added that Uchumi would be a good short term investment because of the announced dividend of 4.0 and a bonus issue of one share for every two shares held.
"Unless inflation is maintained at the current low level, in the long term the price may go down because so much of its profits depend on consumers' purchasing power," a broker said.
